extension.description: Automatically mutes bad words during video playback using subtitle timing. Works with local files and streaming add-ons such as ororo.tv.
extension.disclaimer: Mute accuracy depends on subtitle timing.
extension.news: 1.7.0: - New: scene skipping. When enabled, the add-on jumps past flagged scenes (scary, intense, mature) instead of only muting. Scene windows are read from simple offline skip lists you edit yourself — no subscription or external service needed. - Skip lists live in special://profile/addon_data/service.profanity.filter/skiplists/ and match by movie name (e.g. "Avatar (2009).skip.txt") or global.skip.txt for every video. Format is one "start end" per line (mm:ss / h:mm:ss / plain seconds). A bundled example is included. - New settings: "Enable scene skipping" and "Skip-start lookahead (seconds)". 1.6.1: - Fix streaming subtitle discovery: subtitle URLs with signed query strings (e.g. ororo WebVTT tokens) are now kept intact so downloads no longer fail with auth errors. - Fall back to scanning the full Kodi log when the subtitle URL falls outside the recent log tail. - Adds a "Show detailed failure diagnostics" setting that shows the exact failing stage on screen (player id, whether subtitles became active, URL/download/parse results) so issues are easy to report without reading Kodi's log. 1.6.0: - Subtitles are no longer shown on screen. The filter works with subtitles switched off: local files are read from disk directly (never displayed), and streaming subtitles are only enabled long enough to capture the timing data, then hidden again. - The "Hide subtitles after scanning" setting has been removed — profanity text is always kept off the screen. 1.5.0: - Fix false positives caused by overly greedy wildcards (sh*t no longer matches "shift", c*nt no longer matches "count"). - Ship a curated word list. Innocent/common words (god, hell, abuse, etc.) are no longer muted by default. - Use the active video player for subtitle discovery instead of a hardcoded player id.
